clue.text: Even the score by bribery?

parts.note: levelling a game's tally and buying someone off share one verb, so a single word covers both acts

explanation.surface: A match is levelled by paying someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: To level the scores is to square them, and to square an official is slang for bribing them; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to make equal and, informally, to secure someone's cooperation with a bribe.

clue.text: Behave shiftily before embarking on the deal

explanation.surface: Someone acts evasively before starting a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'deal' is of cards, which are mixed before dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: To shuffle is to move evasively or prevaricate, and to mix a pack of cards before dealing them.

clue.text: Dressed, or nude and natural

indicators.note: dressed means prepared or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A choice between clothed or naked and unspoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' looks like a definition, the very opposite of the answer, but it signals the anagram of OR NUDE AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Unadorned means plain, without decoration, and so simple and natural.

clue.text: A number in the arena competing in track events

indicators.note: the first pieces sit within the arena word

parts.note: a ring is an arena, as for boxing or circus
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Athletes in an arena take part in track events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' suggests a contestant's number, but it is the Roman numeral C.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking part in contests of speed on a track is what running or riding in races means.

clue.text: Don't give up project

explanation.surface: Advice to persist with a piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere to the end is to stick it out; something that protrudes or projects is said to stick out.

clue.text: Bite from upset insect

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a gnat is a small biting insect

explanation.surface: An insect turned over delivers a bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bite' suggests an insect bite, but here it means a sharp taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A tang is a sharp, piquant flavour, which is also what bite means in food.

clue.text: The monkey's brother

explanation.surface: A remark about a monkey's sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: 's' stands for 'is'; 'brother' means a friar, not a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American monkey is named for its cowl-like head; a friar of the Franciscan reform order bears the same name.

clue.text: Ring a poor actor up in America

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the words read from bottom to top

parts.note: a ham is a bad, over-the-top actor

explanation.surface: Phoning a bad actor working in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses A HAM to MAHA; 'Ring' suggests a phone call but is O. The definition is loose: a city in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in the US state of Nebraska.

clue.text: Withdraw escort

explanation.surface: Pulling out of a date.
explanation.definitionFit: To take out money is to withdraw it; to take someone out is to escort them on an outing.

clue.text: Period for redemption: we object to article by church

parts.note: the object (accusative) form of the pronoun we is us
an is the indefinite article
CE is short for Church of England

explanation.surface: A protest against an article about the church's view of redemption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we object' looks like a protest but asks for the grammatical object form of 'we'. USANCE is the time allowed for paying a foreign bill of exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: Usance is the customary period allowed before a bill of exchange must be paid or redeemed.

clue.text: We hear sleeping bag is carried by hikers

indicators.note: a heard-it-said signal: the word for sleeping is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: taking a nap is sleeping briefly
a sack is a bag

explanation.surface: A sleeping bag forms part of a hiker's load.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a thing carried by hikers. NAP said aloud gives KNAP, with a silent K.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack strapped to the back is standard luggage for walkers on a trail.

clue.text: Basically, a threat needs to be dealt with

indicators.note: dealt with suggests the letters are handled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Fundamentally, a threat must be tackled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs to be dealt with' signals the anagram of A THREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: At heart means fundamentally, in one's essential nature.

clue.text: An additional comment provided by the organist

definitions.text: An additional comment provided by the organist

parts.words: An additional comment provided by the organist
parts.note: an organist plays bass notes on pedals with the feet, which gives a second reading of a remark printed at the bottom of a page

explanation.surface: A musician adds a remark to a document.
explanation.walkthrough: An organ has a pedalboard, so some of its notes are literally played by foot.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra remark placed below the main text of a page bears this name; the organist's pedal sounds are the pun.

clue.text: Volume of tax return accepted by firm starting with nothing

indicators.note: says the piece for nothing comes at the front of the answer

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

indicators.note: one piece is taken inside another, as a guest is accepted into a house

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: a tax return here signals that the word for tax is read backwards

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A book about a company's tax return, written from scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' makes TAV from VAT, and 'accepted by' places it in CO; 'starting with' puts O at the front. 'tax return' reads as accountancy.
explanation.definitionFit: An octavo is a book size, made by folding each printed sheet into eight leaves, so a volume of that format.

clue.text: Shone like a newly minted medal, for example?

indicators.note: freshly minted means newly made, so the letters are recast

parts.note: eg is short for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Something shone like a freshly struck medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly minted' signals the anagram of MEDAL plus EG; 'like' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To gleam is to glow brightly or reflect light, just as polished metal does.

clue.text: Turnback before it erupts

indicators.note: printed as one word, turn back tells us the word for before is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A warning to retreat before an eruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnback' turns ANTE round; the volcano in Sicily is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, famous for frequent eruptions.

clue.text: It provides food with tea, milk etc free

indicators.note: the letters are set free to form a new order

explanation.surface: An offer of food with free tea, milk and other extras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like the price but signals the anagram of TEA MILK ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal ticket is literally a voucher for food, and figuratively a source of reliable support.

clue.text: Learning to recognise that student has the advantage

parts.note: to know a face is to recognise it
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
an edge is an advantage over rivals

explanation.surface: Learning to spot when a student has an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: L for a learner comes from the L-plates on a British learner driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge is what one acquires through learning, as in a person of great learning.

clue.text: May be carelessly dropped in the middle of nowhere

definitions.text: May be carelessly dropped in the middle of nowhere

parts.words: May be carelessly dropped in the middle of nowhere
parts.note: the middle letter of the word nowhere is H, a breathed sound some speakers carelessly drop

explanation.surface: Something left behind carelessly in a remote spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the middle of nowhere' suggests a remote place but means the H at the centre of 'nowhere'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirate is the breathed H sound, which careless speakers drop, as in 'ospital'.

clue.text: Train speed is reduced to walking pace

indicators.note: the words are broken down and rebuilt, as something reduced is taken apart

explanation.surface: A train's speed slows to a crawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is reduced' signals the anagram of TRAIN SPEED; 'to' is a link. A pedestrian pace is a walking one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian describes going on foot, and figuratively anything slow and plodding.

clue.text: A show presented before the show

definitions.text: A show presented before the show

parts.words: A show presented before the show
parts.note: a screening given ahead of the official opening of a play or film

explanation.surface: A performance staged before the main performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A preview is a showing for an audience before the official opening or release.

clue.text: African wasteland

explanation.surface: A barren stretch of land in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A Moor is a North African Muslim of Berber or Arab descent; a moor is open uncultivated upland.

clue.text: Appreciate consideration

explanation.surface: Valuing thoughtful treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect someone is to esteem them; respect is also regard or consideration for others.

clue.text: What many, in panic, make themselves

definitions.text: What many, in panic, make themselves

parts.words: What many, in panic, make themselves
parts.note: frightened people quickly get out of the way, as in the idiom about vanishing from a scene

explanation.surface: People in a panic do this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make yourself scarce' is an idiom meaning leave quickly or disappear.
explanation.definitionFit: To make oneself scarce is to slip away or hide, as panicked crowds do.

clue.text: Dulcie bad in geometry

indicators.note: the name is treated badly, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A girl called Dulcie is poor at geometry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' signals the anagram of DULCIE; the definition is loose, naming the Greek whose Elements founded the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alexandrian mathematician wrote the Elements and is known as the father of that branch of mathematics.

clue.text: Fur covering one animal

parts.note: an animal's coat is its covering of fur
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An animal's fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The coati is a raccoon-like mammal of the Americas with a long snout.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a South American mammal of the raccoon family.

clue.text: Labour candidate -he's accepted dirty money that must be returned

indicators.note: one piece takes in the other, as a bribe is accepted

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: the dirty money is returned, so its word is read backwards

parts.note: filthy lucre is money got dishonestly

explanation.surface: A Labour Party candidate has taken a bribe that must be repaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that must be returned' turns LUCRE round to make ERCUL. 'Labour' is not the British political party but the Twelve Labours of the Greek hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek strongman was set twelve labours, so he was the one chosen to perform them.

clue.text: A number, if loud, irritate

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
taken as written
f is forte, the musical mark for loud

explanation.surface: A loud number may irritate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' suggests a song, but it is the Roman numeral M.
explanation.definitionFit: To miff is to annoy or offend slightly.

clue.text: Very frightened,1 take a short rest before I can reorganise

indicators.note: the earlier pieces stand ahead of the next

parts.note: the clue prints the figure one, which the Roman numeral I represents (or an OCR slip for the pronoun)
a nap is a short sleep

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A frightened person naps before regrouping.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed figure 1 stands where the pronoun I belongs; either way it supplies I. 'reorganise' turns I CAN into ANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: To be gripped by sudden fear and alarm is to be in a state of panic.

clue.text: Violin piece needs quartet to play it

explanation.surface: A violin part needs a string quartet to perform it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quartet' suggests string players, but the card game is played by four.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge is the wooden support for a violin's strings; the card game needs four players.

clue.text: Send away for being a complete failure

explanation.surface: Someone dismissed as an utter flop.
explanation.walkthrough: To send away for goods by post is to write off for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing off by post is ordering something by letter; a wreck or total loss beyond repair is likewise called this.

clue.text: Go easy for about 40 days

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Lent is the forty-day Christian fast before Easter

explanation.surface: Advice to take things gently for about forty days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link here; 'about' is not an approximation but RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To soften or ease off from a harsh stance is to relent.
